subject: Observability activation — ops readiness & knowledge transfer
messages_1_subject: Observability activation — ops readiness & knowledge transfer
messages_1_body:
Hi Soojin & Marissa,

Orion Health confirmed their production cutover window for the week of Feb 27 and asked for an operations/observability handoff this week so their SREs can own runbook-driven incident responses. Key asks from their side: dashboard orientation, tracing hook examples, error taxonomy mapping to their ticketing, and an on-call routing proposal.

I captured the initial checklist (attached) and flagged three items we should own before handoff:
- Dashboard ownership and a list of default panels for P50/P95 latency, error rates, and model fallback counts.
- Trace context propagation example (service -> inference runtime -> cache) and a short patch to include correlating tags.
- Alert routing matrix (who gets page vs. slack notice) + runbook links.

Can you two coordinate a short internal run-through tomorrow, then a 45-minute knowledge-transfer with their SREs on Thursday? I left a rough agenda in the attachment.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0129
messages_2_subject: Re: Observability activation — ops readiness & knowledge transfer
messages_2_body:
Ben — thanks for the heads up. I skimmed the checklist and sketched a smaller activation scope so we can be practical before cutover:
1) Dashboard inventory: produce a single pane with request latency by model variant, error class (client/server/model), and cache hit ratio. I can pull a draft from the instrumentation repo.
2) Tracing hooks: we'll provide a code snippet (Node + Python examples) that shows trace IDs and model-version context. I'll include a small test harness they can run.
3) Error taxonomy: propose a mapping to severity (sev1: data loss/model crash; sev2: throttling/high error rates; sev3: degraded quality). We'll map to their Jira workflow in the knowledge transfer.

Internal sync: 11:00 AM PST tomorrow (Wed) in #cs-onboarding — I invited Marissa. After that I'll prepare the deck + runbook template.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
soojin.lee@redwood.com
messages_3_subject: Re: Observability activation — ops readiness & knowledge transfer
messages_3_body:
Thanks, Ben / Soojin — this looks great.

Thursday at 2:00 PM PST for the knowledge-transfer works for our SREs. Could you include a short section on:
- How Redwood's fallback policies surface as alerts (we see this as a potential source of noisy alerts)
- Example trace that ties user request -> model selection -> latency spike -> fallback
- A recommended set of thresholds for initial alerting (we can tune after cutover)

We'll circulate our on-call rotation and Jira project key (OPS-230) prior to the call.

Elena Park
Director of Platform Engineering, Orion Health
elena.park@orionhealth.io
messages_4_body:
Forwarding the draft artifacts we'll use in Thursday's session. Quick notes:
- Attached: dashboard-inventory.xlsx (sheet 'Recommended') and runbook-template.md.
- Agenda (45m): 10m dashboard tour, 10m tracing demo (live), 10m error taxonomy + mapping to OPS-230, 10m alert routing + next steps, 5m Q&A.

Elena — during the tracing demo we'll show a minimal diff that adds two tags: redwood.trace_id and model.version. That lets you route traces directly into your existing observability pipeline.

Ben — following the call we'll create a short action item list and assign owners. I can own the dashboard panel PR and Soojin can own the runbook commit.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
messages_5_subject: Post-call: action items and runbook PRs
messages_5_body:
Thanks everyone for the session earlier — good momentum. Summary + owners: 

1) Dashboard PR (Marissa) — add P50/P95 latency by model variant, error-rate panel, cache hit ratio. Target: PR by EOD Wed.
2) Tracing snippets (Soojin) — Node & Python examples + small harness. I'll open a git branch and attach the patch.
3) Runbook (Soojin) — initial runbook created (runbook-template.md attached in thread). We'll include severity mapping to OPS-230 and link to the alert playbook.
4) Alert routing (Ben) — propose initial routing: page SRE on sev1, notify on-call of sev2 via Slack, create Jira ticket for sev3.

Attachments: obs-activation-checklist.pdf, runbook-template.md.

Next step: I'll create the PRs and ping your OPS channel when ready. If you want a separate dry-run incident on Feb 25, say so and we'll run through the playbook.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
soojin.lee@redwood.com
